title: Fluorescent Metal–Organic Frameworks for Chemical Sensing: Design Strategies, Mechanisms, and Analytical Applications
abstract: Fluorescent metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) have emerged as transformative platforms for chemical sensing, combining ultrahigh porosity, tunable optical properties, and versatile host-guest chemistry to achieve exceptional sensitivity and selectivity. This review synthesizes recent advances (2018-2025, with emphasis on 2021-2025) in the design, synthesis, and application of luminescent MOF sensors for environmental monitoring, biomedical diagnostics, and food safety.

title: On again, off again: thiol-Michael photoactivated dynamic covalent chemistry
abstract: Light-responsive dynamic covalent chemistry is a powerful tool that can provide spatiotemporal control of dynamic bond exchange when coupled with light as an external stimulus. Despite its promise, there is a need to develop new tools to harness light for controlling dynamic covalent chemistry. Here, we report a new strategy that couples a traditional coumarin photoremovable protecting group with a thiol-Michael dynamic covalent system at the site of photoactivation. This coumarin Michael acceptor undergoes traditional thiol-Michael exchange on the ground state.

title: Impact of Chronic Hydration–Dehydration Cycling on Enamel Analog Microhardness and Crack Propagation: An in Vitro Model of Dry Environmental Stress
abstract: Objective: To evaluate the effects of repeated hydration–dehydration cycles on the mechanical integrity of enamel analog materials, focusing on microhardness reduction and crack propagation behavior under simulated dry conditions. Methods: Commercial hydroxyapatitebased enamel analog discs (n = 60; diameter 6 mm, thickness 2 mm; Sigma-Aldrich) were subjected to controlled hydration–dehydration cycles over 14 days. Four groups were established: Control (constant hydration), Mild (1 cycle/day), Moderate (3 cycles/day), and Sustained (6 cycles/day).

title: Continuous Flow Electrophotochemical Minisci Reaction via Catalytic Benzophenone Regeneration
abstract: The use of benzophenone as a hydrogen atom transfer (HAT) photocatalyst is limited by catalyst deactivation through ketyl radical dimerization, often requiring stoichiometric loadings. Herein, we report a continuous flow electrophotochemical strategy that enables its catalytic use via in situ regeneration from benzopinacol. This approach relies on a simple single-pass reactor that integrates photochemical activation with electrochemical turnover.

title: Extending Generative Machine Learning for Sustainable Polymer Design: An Integrated Workflow from Generative Models to Bio-Based Candidates
abstract: The discovery of sustainable bio-based polymers is a pressing need, as traditional synthetic polymers derived from fossil fuels pose significant environmental challenges. However, bio-based alternatives often occupy different regions of chemical space and typically lack the mechanical and thermal performance of their synthetic counterparts. In this study, we present a generative machine learning pipeline to design and predict the properties of novel polymers, with current validation on synthetic datasets and future extension to bio-based systems.

title: Parallel Evolution of Dirhodium Artificial Metalloenzymes Creates Distinct Reaction Environments for Selective Carbene Transfer
abstract: Artificial metalloenzymes (ArMs) combine the reactivity of transition metal catalysts with the selectivity and evolvability of protein scaffolds. Understanding different mechanisms by which scaffolds can impart selectivity would greatly facilitate ArM design efforts. In this study, we conducted parallel directed evolution prolyl oligopeptidase (POP)-based dirhodium ArMs toward two mechanistically distinct carbene insertion reactions, N-H and Si-H insertion, to study differences in their stereoselectivity and reaction specificity.

title: FluoFlow as a Family-anchored fragment flow matching for near-infrared fluorophore candidate discovery
abstract: Generative models could accelerate fluorophore discovery, but wavelength conditioning is difficult when red and near-infrared emitters occupy sparse, family-structured regions of chemical space. We introduce FluoFlow, a fragment-tree flow-matching workflow that combines emissionband conditioning with chemically meaningful family-anchor decoding. Across three seeds, unconstrained generation produced strictly monotonic but compressed responses to 450, 550, 650 and 720 nm targets, with a mean 720–450 nm predicted-emission slope of 74.1 ± 16.5 nm.

title: Utility of Acid Co-Product from Bipolar Membrane Electrodialysis as a Function of System-scale, Location, and Flexible Operation
abstract: Bipolar membrane electrodialysis (BPMED) produces acid and base from seawater, and is being primarily advanced for base generation, with co-produced acid needing valorization. Acid cost and utility depend on process scale, electricity prices, and industrial context. Colocating BPMED with desalination facilities and operating flexibly can reduce production costs.

title: Influence of the surface Rock-Salt Layer in Ni-rich NMC cathodes
abstract: Rock-Salt Layer (RSL) formation is one of the main degradation processes in Nirich cathodes for Li-ion batteries, giving rise to loss of capacity and cyclability. Our combined theory and experimental study examines in detail the impact of different compositions of the RSL that form on the surface of Ni-rich cathodes. We confirm the morphology of our RSL models by reproducing the RSL peak observed in experiments in the oxygen K-edge X-ray absorption spectra. Wannier-based charge analysis reveals the impact of the RSL in forming a preventive coating towards oxygen loss.

title: Simple and reproducible ready-to-use TMB solution for enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay
abstract: The enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) is a cornerstone of modern laboratory diagnostics, yet its routine implementation is often constrained by the cost and logistics of chromogenic substrates. While commercial 3,3',5,5'-tetramethylbenzidine (TMB) solutions offer superior stability, their high price is a significant burden. Conversely, standard laboratory preparations are inexpensive but suffer from poorly characterized stability, necessitating daily preparation.

title: Guiding photochemical process intensification through kinetic diagnostics
abstract: Photochemical methodologies are commonly optimized towards yield, yet yield alone provides limited insight into productivity and scalability. Here, we demonstrate how simple kinetic diagnostics can guide photochemical process intensification by identifying the dominant limitations governing reaction performance. Using the photochemical Minisci alkylation of phenanthridine with ethane as a representative gas-liquid transformation, systematic screening of pressure, mixing, light intensity, and temperature revealed the controlling transport and kinetic phenomena, enabling targeted engineering…

title: Excited Triplet States during Organofluorine Molecular Dynamics upon Electron-Impact—A Study of Electronic Structure and Molecular Fragmentation
abstract: The semiconductor industry’s reliance on high global warming potential (GWP) perfluorocarbon etchants motivates the search for environmentally sustainable alternatives. Although exchange scattering populates triplet states efficiently during electron-impact excitation, computational studies of organofluorine etchant fragmentation have been largely confined to the ground state or to static potential energy surface scans, leaving triplet-state dissociation dynamics essentially uncharacterised.

title: Visible range sub band gap photoexcitation of conductivehydrogenated nanodiamonds
abstract: Hydrogenated milled nanodiamonds (H-MND) are emerging as original candidates for photocatalysis applications, demonstrating notably outstanding performances for PFOA degradation in water under solar-type illumination. However, the involved sub-band gap photoexcitation mechanisms remain poorly understood, as the material's electronic properties, such as its electron affinity, surface states, and Fermi level depend on both its surface chemistry and its interface with solvent.

title: Accurate 20 ms protein sizing with microscope‑based dynamic light scattering
abstract: Dynamic Light Scattering (DLS) is a powerful technique to probe nano to microscale objects in solution. Among its main limitations is the requirement of steady-state conditions during measurement, restricting its applicability towards time evolving systems. Here, we present a microscopy-based DLS approach using oblique illumination to significantly enhance the signal-to-background ratio compared to conventional confocal geometries. The coherence factor 𝛽 of the autocorrelation function increases to values above 0.9, approaching the ideal limit.

title: Dual Digital Twins for Experimental Planning in Automated Laboratories: Physics-informed surrogate models for counterfactual experimental rollouts
abstract: Automated laboratories increasingly combine automated and cloudified instruments, robotic operation, sample provenance and data infrastructures, and autonomous agents. Yet these capabilities primarily address execution, while planning remain limited to myopic optimization workflows or generic agentic approaches. At the same time, open decision-making algorithms such as MCDTs, reinforcement learning, or dynamic programming that worked exceptionally well for AlphaFold and MuZero are very limited for experimental scenarios due to extreme data requirements.

title: Interpretable machine learning reveals physicochemical drivers of bio-crude yield in hydrothermal liquefaction of water hyacinth
abstract: Hydrothermal liquefaction (HTL) is a promising pathway for converting wet biomass into biocrude oil; however, the complex interactions among process parameters limit mechanistic understanding and optimization. In this study, an interpretable machine learning framework was developed to predict and analyze bio-crude yield from the HTL of water hyacinth using a curated dataset of 69 experimental observations.

title: All-Photonic Yellow-Red-Blue-Green Orthogonal Photoswitching for Rewritable Four-Color 2D and 3D Displays and Optical Memories
abstract: Light-induced color change is the defining and most fundamental characteristic of a photochromic material. Twofold switching between colorless and color or two different colors is known to humanity for centuries and has been used allegedly already in antiquity by Alexander the Great to coordinate troop movements. Today, the two-color changes of photochromes cover the whole visible spectrum. However, the next logical step of multicolor combinations has proven to be extremely difficult, and a basic four-color system is particularly challenging to realize in a fully photonic fashion.

title: Elucidating mobile charge carriers in polymeric carbon nitrides by transient surface photovoltage analysis
abstract: Understanding charge carrier dynamics in granular photocatalysts is critical for rational materials design, yet conventional spectroscopies lack the spatial directionality needed to distinguish individual electron and hole contributions. Here, time-resolved surface photovoltage (TRSPV) spectroscopy is established as a contactless, carrier-resolved probe of charge transport in granular photoactive materials, using undoped and sulfur-doped polymeric carbon nitride (PCN) as model systems.

title: TD-DCC: An Interactive and Efficient Graphical User Interface-Based Time-Dependent Cross-Correlation Analysis from Molecular Dynamics Trajectories
abstract: Dynamic cross-correlation matrix (DCCM) analysis is a widely used method for inferring correlated motions in biological macromolecules from molecular dynamics (MD) trajectories. Conventional implementations often result in a single time-averaged matrix from the entire trajectory. Thus, time-dependent cross-correlations between residues of interest and their oscillations are often difficult to analyze. Also, transient correlations are difficult to probe using the DCCM. This information is crucial for interpreting allosteric communication in bio-macromolecules.

title: Chlorinated Byproducts in Diisocyanates Synthesis from 35Cl NQR
abstract: Chlorinated impurities in industrial diisocyanates production significantly impact product quality and stability, yet their speciation remains an analytical challenge. This study demonstrates that 35Cl NQR spectroscopy, supported by DFT calculations, provides a powerful framework for identifying byproducts in these processes. We show that NQR frequencies effectively categorize chlorinated species—such as amino hydrochlorides and carbamoyl chlorides—into distinct chemical families, with signal shifts driven by local electronic structure, intermolecular interactions, and conformation.

title: Quantifying Fragment Ambiguity inLC-ESI-HRMS-MS2 Spectral Databases
abstract: LC–MS/HRMS-based non-target analysis relies heavily on MS2 spectral matching for compound annotation. However, not all fragments contribute equally to identification confidence, and quantitative measures of fragment ambiguity remain lacking. In this study, we developed a data-driven probabilistic framework to assess fragment level diagnostic power through the Fragment Ambiguity Score (FAS), which combines fragment stability and specificity within precursor-mass-defined candidate spaces.

title: Obtaining Dynamics of Supported Metal Nanoparticles using Cost-effective Training of Machine Learning Force Fields
abstract: Metal–support interactions (MSI) play a critical role in heterogeneous catalysis by influencing catalyst stability and reactivity. A long-term objective is to model catalytic systems in simulated experiments, to obtain atomistic insights into MSI under reaction conditions. Achieving this goal requires extensive modelling of large atomistic systems. Machine-learned force fields (MLFF’s) enable simulations at these scales by providing orders of magnitude speedups compared to density functional theory (DFT).

title: In situ salt-loaded cathode by mechanochemical modification for pre-metallation of next-generation metal-ion capacitors
abstract: Metal-ion capacitors (MICs) as hybrid devices stand out for their high energy and power output. Their Achilles’ heel, however, is the mandatory pre-metallation, which is essential for the device to operate at its best. Depending on the chosen strategy, it results in safety issues, suffering in performance and time-consuming preparation. Herein, we present a holistic approach overcoming these limitations by mechanochemical in situ modification of sacrificial salts to provide additional metal-ions.

title: Unexpected Photochemical Synthesis of Unsubstituted AzaBenzannulated Perylenediimides and Bisazacoronene
abstract: Unsubstituted nitrogen-doped coronene diimides (CDIs), named bisazacoronene diimides (uBACDs), were unexpectedly obtained by exposing perylene diimides (PDIs) linked to a pyrrole or furan derivative via an imine bond in their bay region. This cleavage depends on the presence of molecular oxygen: performing the same transformation in an oxygen-free environment yields the non-cleaved, functionalized azabenzannulated product.

title: A Synergistic Multimodal DEL-Driven Strategy with In Silico Guidance for SARS-CoV-2 PLpro Inhibitor Discovery
abstract: The SARS-CoV-2 papain-like protease (PLpro) is a pivotal antiviral target due to its essential roles in viral replication and host immune evasion. Here, we report a synergistic, multimodal strategy driven by DNA-encoded libraries (DEL) and integrated with in silico guidance for the efficient discovery of novel PLpro inhibitors. This approach combines focused DEL screening, photo-crosslinking DEL for privileged fragment identification, and focused virtual screening, all guided by iterative rounds of X-ray crystallography and structure-based optimization.

title: Mobility Suppression Boundary Principle for Polymer Glass-Transition Temperature
abstract: Polymer glass-transition temperature (Tg) varies widely even among repeat units with similar visible chemistry and size. This manuscript formulates and tests the Mobility Suppression Boundary Principle (MSBP-Tg): within comparable chemistry-size fibers, upward Tg boundary displacement is associated with suppression of normalized local rotatable mobility. The density coordinate used here is exactly the sign reversal of rotatable-bond density, MSBP density = -NumRotatableBonds/heavy_atoms. Thus the contribution is not the invention of a new molecular descriptor.

title: Tall oil pitch as a graphite feedstock: direct conversion of a biomassderived by-product into bulk graphite
abstract: Tall oil pitch (TOP), a high-boiling by-product obtained from crude tall oil refining in the kraft pulping process, was converted into bulk graphite through catalyst-free thermal treatment. This result demonstrates that a biomass-derived industrial residue can serve directly as a feedstock for graphite. Without catalysts or prior purification, thermal treatment of TOP produced bulk graphite, as confirmed by Raman spectroscopy and X-ray diffraction. The results indicate that graphite can be generated from multicomponent resin-derived residues through simple thermal processing.

title: An efficient selective synthesis of E isomers of di-SF4-vinyl fluorides from pyridine-SF4-acetylene in presence of Triethyl borane.
abstract: The synthesis of vinyl fluorides plays a crucial role in various scientific disciplines, including pharmaceutical and materials sciences. In this study, first time we present a direct and stereoselective method for the synthesis E isomers of Di-SF4-vinyl fluorides from pyridine-SF4-acetylene, in which the two heterocycles are connected by a rodlike trans-di-SF4 alkene linker, via the regioselective free radical addition, dehalogenation and followed by hydrogenation of pyridine–SF4–acetylene and Aromatic & Hetero aromatic SF4Cl in the presence of triethyl borane.

title: Demonstration of a Thermodynamic Cycle for Interpreting Cation-driven Tuning of Redox Chemistry
abstract: Although it has been established that the properties of molecules and materials can be tuned via incorporation of secondary cations, a rigorous thermodynamic framework for interpreting the origins of such effects has remained elusive. Here, a thermodynamic cycle for cation-driven tuning is proposed that describes the fundamental relationship between shifts in the association constants of cations and shifts in reduction potentials.

title: Predicting Amide-I Infrared Spectra Directly from Coarse-Grained Protein Simulations
abstract: Theoretical vibrational spectroscopy methods are often necessary to interpret condensed-phase spectra. For some methods, such as those that use vibrational spectroscopic maps, the requisite atomistic molecular dynamics simulations can become prohibitively expensive for systems of interest. Here, we present a two-stage method for predicting amide-I region infrared spectra from coarse-grained protein simulations, which reduces the computational cost of spectral prediction.

title: Systematic Exploration of the Ternary Dy–Ir–Sn System with Magnetic Property Investigation
abstract: The ternary Dy–Ir–Sn system phase equilibria were investigated with a goal of identifying novel phases. Samples were prepared by arc-melting and subsequent annealing, then characterized using scanning electron microscopy, powder X-ray diffraction, and single crystal X-ray diffraction. To streamline the exploratory process, a scalable, high-throughput framework was developed to automate the summary of crystallographic data, which aids the systematic exploration of ternary intermetallic systems and provides a reproducible methodology for exploratory materials characterization.

title: Acyl-Chain Unsaturation in the Cremimycin Macrolactam Yields Cremimycin B with
Production of Metallophores Rhodopetrobactin B and Methylolanthanin in Methylobacterium extorquens strains PA1 and AM1
abstract: The closely related M. extorquens strains PA1 and AM1 carry near-identical metallophore synthesis gene clusters, yet AM1 produces the 4-hydroxy benzoate (4HB)-capped chelator methylolanthanin (MLL), while PA1 produces mainly 3,4-dihydroxy benzoate (3,4-DHB)-capped rhodopetrobactin (RPB) siderophores. We trace this divergence to a single tandem-duplication frameshift that inactivates AsbF, the dehydratase supplying the catecholate precursor 3,4-DHB.

title: Hierarchically Porous Nanoparticle-based Aerogels with Engineered Backbone Porosity for Enhanced Stability and Functionality
abstract: Precise control over the structural architecture of aerogels remains a central challenge, particularly for integrating well-defined nanoscale porosity within the aerogel backbone. Here, a nanoparticleassembly strategy is presented for fabricating aerogels with controlled backbone porosity using preformed mesoporous silica nanoparticles (MSNs) as building blocks. This approach decouples network formation from pore generation, enabling independent control over composition, structure, and porosity.

title: Cross-exposure transferability and failure boundaries of self-supervised DNN denoising for AR-HAXPES depth profiling
abstract: Laboratory-source angle-resolved hard X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (AR-HAXPES) is photon-starved at the spatial resolution required for mapping, where the frame averaging needed to recover a clean depth profile at every position drives total acquisition time into a prohibitive regime. Self-supervised deep-neural-network (DNN) denoising offers an alternative to acquisition-time scaling, and a recent companion study has systematically benchmarked its performance against alternative strategies; however, its operational envelope across exposures, its cross-exposure transferability, and its…

title: Programming local confinements in crystalline frameworks through reticular chemistry

Thermographic Digital Twin for Proactive Fire-Risk Prediction in Legacy Residential Electrical Installations: A Systematic Review and Transferability Framework for Ageing Housing and Buildings in Peru
abstract: Residential fires of electrical origin represent a growing public-safety risk in dwellings with ageing installations, in both high-income and middle-income contexts. Reactive approaches based on periodic inspection and conventional alarm systems detect risk only after a fault has already manifested or a fire is under way. This work presents a systematic review of the literature on infrared thermography, digital twins, and machine learning applied to the prediction of electrical faults, with the purpose of synthesising the state of the art and proposing a conceptual predictive thermographic…

title: Development and validation of an interpretable machine learning-based predictive model for breast cancer bone metastasis
abstract: BackgroundBreast cancer is one of the most common malignancies worldwide, with bone metastasis representing its most frequent distant metastatic form, significantly worsening patient prognosis. This study aims to develop a machine learning-based predictive model for accurately assessing the risk of bone metastasis in breast cancer patients, thereby enabling personalized risk stratification, early clinical intervention, and optimized treatment strategies.MethodsThis study utilized the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results database as the primary data source to develop machine learning models for predicting bone metastasis risk in breast cancer patients. Initially, univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses were conducted to screen key predictive variables; subsequently, eight machine learning algorithms were constructed based on the screening results.10-fold cross-validation employed for hyperparameter optimization. Following training, model performance was evaluated on an internal test cohort and externally validated on 342 real-world cases from an independent hospital cohort. Model assessment incorporated multiple metrics, including area under the curve (AUC), area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC), decision curve analysis, and calibration curves. Additionally, SHAP analysis was applied to enhance model interpretability, and a web-based calculator was developed based on the optimal model to facilitate clinical application and decision support.ResultsBaseline characteristics across cohorts indicated that the majority of patients were aged over 50 years, female, predominantly with the HR+/HER2- molecular subtype, and exhibited a low incidence of bone metastasis. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses identified key independent risk factors, including age >50 years, higher tumor grade, advanced T stage, N stage, clinical stage and HR-/HER2- subtype factors included radiotherapy, surgery, and married status. The LGB model demonstrated superior performance, achieving an AUC of 0.98 in the training set and 10-fold cross-validation (standard deviation=0.00), 0.98 in the internal validation set, and 0.91 in the external validation set; AUPRC values across the three cohorts were 0.96, 0.79, and 0.87, respectively; decision curve analysis showed excellent net clinical benefit within the 0.1-0.8 threshold range; calibration curves further confirmed high concordance between predicted probabilities and actual event rates. SHAP analysis highlighted surgery as the primary protective factor, followed by N stage, T stage, and radiotherapy as risk enhancers; for example, advanced N stage was associated with positive SHAP values, indicating a significant increase in bone metastasis risk.ConclusionsThis study developed an interpretable LGB model accompanied by a web-based calculator, thereby advancing personalized risk stratification, early detection of bone metastasis and optimized treatment strategies.

title: Sodium Aluminate as a Water-Soluble Interfacial Modifier Coupling High-Temperature CO2 Retention and Ni Stabilization in Methane Dry Reforming
abstract: Dry reforming of methane (DRM) demands catalysts that simultaneously resist coking and sintering at high temperature. Here, we show that sodium aluminate (NaAlO2) acts as a highly effective interfacial modifier, creating a functional Ni−NaAlO2 metal−support contact that couples reaction-relevant CO2 retention with robust Ni stabilization. Temperature-programmed desorption reveals that NaAlO2 retains CO2-derived species up to 700 °C, driven by the strong basicity of its ionic Na−Al−O lattice, while structural analysis confirms strong interfacial metal−support coupling that preserves the size of metallic Ni. In situ spectroscopy reveals a bifunctional perimeter pathway under DRM conditions, where these CO2-derived oxygen-containing species hosted on NaAlO2 efficiently oxidize CHx intermediates generated on adjacent metallic Ni sites. These coupled interfacial functions enable stable, near-coke-free DRM operation with suppressed Ni sintering for 110 h on stream, drastically outperforming a reference Ni/Al2O3 catalyst that deactivates via severe sintering, coking, and reactor blockage within 24 h. Crucially, NaAlO2 dissolves in water and undergoes reversible hydration/dehydration, enabling uniform post-synthetic deposition onto pre-formed Ni catalysts via a simple aqueous impregnation−drying step. We demonstrate that this modular interface incorporation successfully upgrades both a commercial Ni reforming catalyst and a reference Ni/Al2O3 catalyst without rebuilding the parent catalyst structures, significantly improving their coke and sintering resistance. Overall, this work establishes NaAlO2 as a deployable interfacial modifier for coupled CO2 handling and metal stabilization in practical reforming applications.

title: Decoupling functional group effects on uranium adsorption in UiO-66 through density functional theory and neural network modeling
abstract: The vast uranium resources in seawater provide a sustainable foundation for nuclear energy development. These abundant resources also offer a potential solution to long-term uranium supply challenges caused by dwindling terrestrial reserves and increasing ecological pressures. Therefore, developing high-performance adsorbent materials is essential for the efficient and selective extraction of U(VI) from seawater.

venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Crystal structure and basic properties of dirhenate quantum materials
abstract: The anhydrous divalent 3d-metal dirhenate quantum materials, M(ReO$_4$)$_2$,were synthesized using solid-state methods for M = Mn through Zn. Previously unreported Mg(ReO4)2 is also described. Their layered crystal structures, which feature an in-plane triangular lattice of M$^{2+}$, were refined using single crystal X-ray diffraction, and their optical absorption and several other physical properties were characterized. Their magnetism and heat capacity reveal long-range magnetic order at low temperatures in many of the M(ReO$_4$)$_2$ phases. Notably, many of these ordered states are sensitive to applied magnetic fields and can be readily suppressed by relatively small fields, suggesting competing magnetic interactions in a low-dimensional framework, which appear worthy of further study.

title: Electron-beam Writing of Spectrally Uniform Green Single-photon Emitters in Hexagonal Boron Nitride
abstract: Scalable quantum photonic technologies require single-photon emitters whose positions and emission energies can be engineered simultaneously. Hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) is an attractive room-temperature host, but deterministic creation of spectrally reproducible emitters remains challenging. Here, we use a standard scanning electron microscope as a direct-writing tool to activate bright green single-photon emitters in hBN at predefined sites, without ion implantation or post-fabrication thermal annealing. The written emitters exhibit reproducible zero-phonon-line emission centered near 536 nm, room-temperature antibunching with g(2)(0) as low as 0.08, high brightness, strong linear polarization, and stable emission. Thickness-dependent activation, stacking experiments, cathodoluminescence spectroscopy, and first-principles calculations support a carbon-related defect complex as the most plausible origin of the emission. As a proof of nanophotonic compatibility, we further activate emitters in a nanoparticle-on-mirror plasmonic nanocavity and observe photoluminescence enhancement accompanied by shortened emission lifetimes. These results establish electron-beam direct writing as a practical route to site-selective, spectrally uniform green quantum emitters in hBN, offering a promising basis for integrated room-temperature quantum photonic architectures.

title: Poisson-Gamma Modeling of Inter-Relational Dependencies in Dynamic Knowledge Graphs
abstract: Dynamic knowledge graphs are ubiquitous in today's AI applications, as we represent molecular structures, social relationships, and language information using these graph models. As knowledge graphs evolve over time and are often noisy and incomplete, modeling their temporal and relational dependencies becomes crucial for downstream tasks. To address these challenges, this paper proposes PGRE (Poisson-Gamma Relational Evolution), a probabilistic model for modeling inter-relational dependencies in dynamic knowledge graphs. PGRE represents multi-relational temporal links via a Poisson-Bernoulli formulation. It introduces Gamma-distributed latent variables to capture entity-factor associations and cross-relation dependencies mediated by shared latent communities. A Gamma Markov process further models the temporal evolution of these latent variables, enabling principled characterization of relational dynamics. Experiments on benchmark datasets show that PGRE achieves competitive performance in link prediction, particularly in sparse settings, while revealing meaningful relational evolution patterns in dynamic knowledge graphs.

title: On the Design Space of Discrete Diffusion Online Adaptation for Molecular Optimization
abstract: Molecular optimization often starts from a pretrained generative model that captures a broad prior over valid molecular structures. At test time, however, the goal is not to sample from this prior, but to use a limited oracle budget to shift generation toward task-specific high-reward molecules. We study this adaptation problem for discrete diffusion models. Each online round couples several choices. The loop must decide which candidates to evaluate, how rewards become model updates, which feedback to reuse, and how far to move beyond the pretrained prior. These choices have mostly been studied in isolation, leaving open whether they complement one another, become redundant, or interfere inside a full online adaptation loop. We conduct controlled studies across six small-molecule binding-affinity tasks and three protein-fitness tasks. We find that acquisition, reward shaping, and model debiasing provide complementary routes to higher reward, especially for small molecules. Replay further stabilizes learning, while validity penalties keep small-molecule exploration on the valid molecular manifold. Together, these findings point to a practical recipe for feedback-efficient molecular optimization: online fine-tuning with acquisition, reward shaping, debiasing, replay, and validity control. This recipe outperforms offline fine-tuning and inference-time search baselines under matched oracle-call budgets and GPU-hour accounting. The gains are largest when high-reward candidates require larger shifts from the pretrained prior.
